subject: Hosted API renewal — tier amplification, burst window & invoice cadence
messages:
From: Allison Reed <allison@edgecommerce.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: EdgeCommerce Procurement <procure@edgecommerce.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: Hosted API commit review & estimated uplift

Hi Dylan —

We’re beginning our renewal cycle and want to validate options for increasing our hosted API commitment. Current plan is 1.2B tokens/month; engineering expects 2.5B tokens/month by Mar 2027 with a spike window during the Q1 marketing push. Procurement has a few asks before we route to finance:

- Pricing tiers for token consumption after the committed amount (breakpoints and unit rates)
- Whether we can include a temporary burst pocket for three months (up to +40% of commit) without immediate overage charges if usage is within expected ramp profile
- Invoice cadence options (monthly vs quarterly) and PO timing (we need a PO issued by Jan 15)
- Any SLA/latency guarantees tied to the committed capacity and reservation of capacity in region us-west-2

Can you share a MAP and draft SOW we can review with procurement? Attached is our internal renewal request summary (Edge_Renewal_RQ.pdf). We’d like to set a call next week to walk through numbers.

Thanks,
Allison Reed
Head of Platform Partnerships
EdgeCommerce

[Attachment: Edge_Renewal_RQ.pdf]

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Allison Reed <allison@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: EdgeCommerce Procurement <procure@edgecommerce.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 11:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Hosted API commit review & estimated uplift

Allison —

Appreciate the clear context and timeline. We can support the 2.5B/month target and propose two paths depending on EdgeCommerce’s risk tolerance:

1) Stepped commit (recommended): 24-month commitment that starts at 1.5B/mo for the first 3 months, 2.0B/mo for months 4-6, then 2.5B/mo thereafter. Includes a 3-month burst pocket of +40% without immediate overage billing during the ramp (we capture tokens for reporting and only bill overage if sustained beyond the 3-month ramp). We’d provide a 10% discount on committed unit rates in year 1 for the 24-month term.

2) Straight annual uplift: Single 12-month commitment to 2.5B/mo with standard burst policy (overages billed at published tier rates). Lower upfront discount (5%) versus the stepped option.

For both options: we can reserve capacity in us-west-2 and include a latency SLO for the reserved capacity path (p95 targets and fallbacks to multi-region variants if there’s an outage). Invoice cadence: we support monthly invoicing (default) or quarterly invoicing on request — procurement PO by Jan 15 is doable for either path.

I’ve attached a draft MAP that outlines deliverables and milestones and a starting SOW. Can you confirm which option procurement prefers and whether the PO cadence is monthly or quarterly? I can schedule a 30-min call next Tue/Thu to run the finance and ops details.

Next steps:
- Ally confirm preferred path (stepped vs straight)
- I’ll loop in Sales Ops and Legal and send an updated SOW + formal quote

Attachments: Edge_MAP_v1.pdf, SOW-EdgeCommerce-v0.3.docx

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachments: Edge_MAP_v1.pdf, SOW-EdgeCommerce-v0.3.docx]

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: EdgeCommerce renewal — concession request + capacity ops

Folks —

Recap: EdgeCommerce wants to move to 2.5B/mo target by Mar. Procurement timeline requires PO by Jan 15. I proposed two options (stepped 24mo with 10% year-1 concession; straight 12mo with 5% concession). Allison is leaning toward the stepped path but needs formal pricing and a MAP that explicitly calls out the 3-month ramp burst pocket and reporting.

Ops asks / risks:
- We need to reserve capacity in us-west-2 for the committed lanes; confirm availability with infra and tag capacity to the deal to avoid over-provisioning.
- The 3-month burst policy is a product change: we’ll report burst usage but won’t bill overage unless usage is sustained beyond the ramp. Need Finance signoff on how we accrue revenue and document the temporary credit terms.
- Legal: expedite SOW review on the capacity reservation language and fallback model variants.

Pricing ask: can we approve a 10% committed-rate discount in year 1 if they sign a 24-month commit? This will materially help close before EOY procurement cycle and preserves long-term ARR. If Sales Ops prefers, we can trade for a shorter ramp (2 months) or a stricter overage floor.

Ben / Marissa — please advise on approval path (discount authority and revenue recognition) and any guardrail you’d like on the burst pocket. I’ll wait for your cue before sending the formal quote.

Thanks,
Dylan

> On Wed, Dec 9, 2026 at 11:45 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com> wrote:

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear options. Procurement has reviewed and prefers the stepped 24-month path with the 3-month burst pocket. A few clarifications before we sign:

- Please include a monthly usage report template showing committed vs burst vs overage (CSV) so our finance team can reconcile invoices quickly.
- We need the PO to reflect monthly invoicing (Edge prefers monthly cadence).
- Can Legal confirm language that the burst pocket is a temporary ramp accommodation and that overage billing only begins if usage > burst threshold for more than 90 days?
- We’d like the updated SOW and a formal quote by EOD Wed (Dec 16) so procurement can start the PO flow.

I’ve attached our PO draft for reference (PO-Draft-Edge.docx) and added a procurement contact for DocuSign: procurement@edgecommerce.com.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the call on Thu 12/16 at 10:00 PT.

Best,
Allison
